name: Yakrang
dates: dates not given in the source
bio: The book says Yakrang was one of the officers of the Emperor Muhammad Shah (r. 1719–48), who lived in dignity and honour at Delhi. It gives no dates for him.

The one piece given here is drawn from Hindustani Lyrics (London: The Sufi Publishing Society, 1919), in the English verse of Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook. It is a free rendering, not a literal translation, and the original Urdu poem is untitled; it is named here by its first line.

poems.title: O ask not frigid Piety to dwell
poems.author: Yakrang
poems.translator: trans. Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook (1919)
poems.text:
O ask not frigid Piety to dwell
    In the same house with Youth and warm Desire;
It were as idle as if one should tell
    Water to be a comrade of the Fire.

O say not only that the Loved One left
    My lonely heart, and fled beyond recall;
But I of rest and patience am bereft,
    And losing Her I am deprived of all.

Take heed, O Hunter, though within thy net
    Thou hold this bird, my soul, with many bands,
I struggle sore, for Freedom lures me yet,
    And may escape from out thy cruel hands.
